recipes.name: Healthier Southern Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 8 fresh peaches - peeled, pitted, and sliced into thin wedges
6 tablespoons unsalted butter, chilled and cut into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Combine peaches, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, nutmeg, lemon juice, and cornstarch in a large bowl. Toss to coat evenly, and pour into a 2-quart baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine flour, white sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Blend in butter with your fingertips or a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal. Stir in water until just combined.
Remove peaches from oven, and drop spoonfuls of flour mixture over them.
Mix together 2 tablespoons brown sugar and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Sprinkle entire cobbler with the sugar and cinnamon mixture. Bake until topping is golden, about 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I really liked this--just be sure to watch it or it could burn if it bakes too long. It took about 20-25 minutes for our topping to get brown enough, 30 minutes would have been too much. The main thing I liked is that you don't feel like you're eating pure sugar. The peaches shine, and if you wanted to add a small scoop of vanilla ice cream to it you won't blow your diet. Pecans would also make a nice addition. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

Excellent! Just the right amount of sweetness and the topping was delectably light and crisp. I used King Arthur White Whole Wheat Flour and, since I was using what I could salvage from a bunch of seconds/bruised peaches, I went by weight instead of number of peaches. Two pounds does it. And don't bother peeling the peaches, for heaven's sake! Oh, and thick chunks work just fine. :) I will be making two 6-quart pans of this for a community dinner and will report back on making it for a crowd.

Baked at 20 minutes instead of 30. The 425 temp really cooks it up fast. Used fresh Georgia peaches-only the best! Definitely could add some oats in the topping for a little more substance. Most definitely a win for the entire family.

This is SO much better than regular peach cobbler. It doesn't give me that sick feeling from consuming too much sugar. I used honey in place of brown sugar and brown rice flour in place of the cornstarch in the peach mixture. I used half whole wheat and half brown rice flour, 4 TBL vegan butter, and slightly less white sugar in the biscuit mixture. Thanks so much for submitting, I will be using this for apple cobbler also!

I mixed a variety of fruits- 5 peaches needed using up, supplemented with frozen mixed fruits. It only needed 15-20 minutes to bake. I had put the timer on for 25 minutes, but at 20 minutes it was slightly burnt on the tips. Really easy recipe though. Served it up with the low fat Cool Whip.
Used white whole wheat flour instead of pastry flour. Baked 25 minutes in convection oven. Whole family loved it!

My daughter and I went peach picking and when we got home to make this recipe, I discovered that we were out of butter! I substituted unsweetened applesauce and left off the final sprinkle of brown sugar and it turned out amazing! The topping became cake like but very moist and fluffy and not too sweet. It soaked up the juice from the peaches just right. My non-sweet tooth husband loves it as do I. Will make it the same way again.

Wonderful recipe, and uses way less sugar than most. You don't even miss it though. The only change I made was to use fresh grated nutmeg and an additional teaspoon of baking powder to make the topping a bit fluffier. Serve with good quality vanilla ice cream or frozen yogurt-YUM!
Soooo good. I mixed some extra bourbon in with the peaches, and it was super yummy! Cooked for 25 minutes @ 5000 ft elevation.

My husband and I loved it! I used Splenda instead of the sugar and the Splenda brown sugar blend instead of the brown sugar to lower the calories even more. I also had to use frozen peaches, but don't listen to the conversion tables online as I bought much more than I needed. It sure makes dieting a little easier when you can have a treat like this! :-)
Awesome! I thought 425º was too high for my glass dish, so I baked it at 350º for 30 minutes and it was just right.
I made the 1/2 recipe, so easy to make in a 9x5 inch loaf pan for a family of four with vanilla ice cream to top it off on a hot summer day!
I made it with canned peaches
I substituted half of the white sugar for Allulose, and a third of the white flour for oats. It was delicious!
My family loved this. I didn’t have enough peaches so I added blueberries. YUM!! Topping was perfect. Not too sweet but sweet enough. 20-23 minutes in the oven was perfect for a golden brown topping.
I followed the recipe exactly. It was an excellent peach cobbler. This is my new peach cobbler recipe!
Perfect amount of sweetness. I made it vegan by using vegan butter.

This was not my favorite recipe and I usually love the highly rated recipes on the site. 

I felt the consistency was too dry for a cobler and the flour filling overpowered the peaches.
This recipe is great! Even my hubby, who was less than enthusiastic about the whole wheat lived it! I didn't change a thing.
Loved it, but the top looked burnt.
